Paragraph: When Arjuna saw his revered elders, teachers, and kinsmen standing opposite him on the battlefield of Kurukshetra, his limbs gave way, his mouth dried up, his body trembled, and his bow slipped from his hand. Overwhelmed by deep pity and grief, he sank down in his chariot, refusing to fight and declaring that he saw no good in slaying his own family.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna suffers an acute panic attack and ethical paralysis caused by moral dilemma, impending loss, and severe family conflict.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna openly expresses his somatic symptoms, anxiety, and vulnerability to Krishna, seeking guidance rather than acting out impulsively.
Outcome/Resolution: By acknowledging his emotional collapse, Arjuna opens the door for cognitive restructuring and spiritual therapy from Krishna.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Anxiety: Panic attack, Somatic symptoms of terror
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Relationship Challenges (Family): Kinship crisis, Moral burden of family conflict

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Vishada (Spiritual despair acting as a catalyst for self-discovery)
Karpanya-dosha (Weakness of spirit arising from emotional distress)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna's breakdown (Arjuna Vishada Yoga) demonstrates how personal attachment creates spiritual blindness, turning duty into an agonizing dilemma.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: A classic description of somatic panic reactions, trauma response, and decision-making paralysis brought on by extreme acute stress.
